question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-x}, & \,0\le x, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-y}, & \,0\le y, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(0\le X,Y\le 3).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & ={e}^{-x}\cdot {e}^{-y} \\  & ={e}^{-x-y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,\infty )\times [0,\infty ).$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-x-y}, & \,0\le x,\,0\le y \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X,Y\le 3) & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-x-y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{-y}{lim}_{b\to \infty }[{\int }_{0}^{b}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{-y}{lim}_{b\to \infty }[-{e}^{-x}]_{0}^{b}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{-y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[-{e}^{-y}]_{0}^{3} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{e}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
